newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SHC up on state tax concession talk.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SHC up on state tax concession talk.

text.p: Shares in casino operator Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd (SHC) rose more than five percent on Tuesday due to speculation that the New South Wales state government may be close to making its decision on a tax concession for the Sydney casino.
But some analysts said the rise may also be due to buying support after the slide in the casino's shares over the past week.
At 11.50 (0050 GMT), Sydney Harbour Casino shares were 11 cents or 5.34 percent higher on light volume at A$2.17.
"The sector looks pretty flat, so there must be something going on there," one casino analyst said. SHC shares were last at A$2.17 on March 13 and hit a recent low of A$2.02 last Thursday.

SHC is seeking a 10 percent tax rate concession for the high roller market from the government, a rate enjoyed by rival casino operators, Victoria's Crown Ltd, Queensland's Jupiters Ltd and Western Australia's Burswood Property Trust.
A NSW government spokesman was not available for comment.
Brokers have forecast that the share price would rise sharply if the concession was granted by state treasurer Michael Egan.
The Sydney casino has a 12-year monopoly to operate the only legal casino in Australia's largest city but has battled with the NSW government to get a similar rate to the other casinos.
Shares in Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which owns 10 percent of SHC, was up five cents to A$6.80 at 12.00 p.m. (0100 GMT).
U.S. casino operator Showboat Inc O.N has a 15 percent holding after recently selling part of its stake to Packer along with management rights to the casino.
